spec.goal: Align rsnap's macOS permission flow with the real product contract: Screen Recording for all capture, plus Accessibility and Input Monitoring only when scroll capture actually starts, with clear in-app recovery paths for one-shot system prompts.
success_criteria: When Screen Recording access is missing on macOS, tray or hotkey capture attempts do not fail silently.
Normal capture entry points request only Screen Recording just in time and continue only when access is already granted or becomes granted.
Scroll capture defers Accessibility and Input Monitoring checks until the user explicitly enters scroll capture, and then explains why each permission is needed.
Users have a persistent in-app permissions surface that explains current status, one-shot system prompt behavior, and recovery steps without requiring a startup onboarding flow.
Fresh repo-native verification covers the final implementation state, and the packaged .app is rebuilt for local smoke use.
constraints: Keep the change scoped to the current macOS permission contract for rsnap's existing capture and scroll-capture surfaces.
Do not introduce a forced first-launch onboarding sequence before the user attempts capture.
Do not require Accessibility or Input Monitoring for normal region, window, or monitor capture.
Preserve the existing menubar, tray, and hotkey entry points and keep non-macOS behavior unchanged.
Use repo-native cargo make tasks from the repository root before claiming completion.

tasks.title: Map the real macOS permission contract to rsnap's capture flows
tasks.objective: Audit the observed packaged-app prompts, current code paths, and relevant macOS APIs to determine which permissions actually belong to normal capture versus scroll capture.
inputs: Observed packaged-app prompts from local user testing
Current rsnap capture and scroll-capture code paths
Apple SDK/API references for Screen Recording, Accessibility, and listen-event access
outputs: A concrete mapping from each prompt to the feature path that triggers it
A confirmed product contract separating normal capture from scroll capture permissions
verification: Local code paths and the selected macOS permission APIs agree on why each permission appears.

tasks.title: Implement just-in-time gating and persistent recovery paths
tasks.objective: Gate Screen Recording at capture start, defer Accessibility and Input Monitoring to scroll-capture entry, and provide a stable request-then-open fallback when macOS no longer shows the one-shot consent sheet.
inputs: Existing settings window and tray/menubar shell
outputs: A macOS permission helper module covering Screen Recording, Accessibility, and Input Monitoring
Just-in-time gating in the shared capture entry point and scroll-capture entry point
A persistent in-app Permissions surface and menu entrypoints
verification: Normal capture reaches OverlaySession::start only when Screen Recording access is available, and scroll capture enables external input only after its extra permissions succeed.

tasks.title: Update durable docs and startup recovery behavior
tasks.objective: Document the real permission contract and keep the menubar-only app visibly recoverable by opening Settings when Screen Recording is missing at startup.
inputs: Current README and v0 spec text
outputs: Updated README and spec text matching the actual permission contract
Startup behavior that opens rsnap Settings when Screen Recording is still missing
verification: The in-app UI and docs explicitly distinguish normal capture from scroll capture requirements.

tasks.title: Run repo-native verification and rebuild the packaged app
tasks.objective: Run the required verification commands against the final implementation, validate the saved plan artifact, and rebuild the macOS app for local smoke testing.
outputs: Fresh repo-native checks, plan-validation evidence, and bundle-build evidence
verification: The saved plan validates as plan/1 JSON

triggers: A new macOS release changes which permission category or system prompt is used for screen capture or listen-event access.
rsnap changes scroll capture to stop observing global scroll input or stop reposting scroll into the target app, which would change the required permission set.
Verification shows the selected delayed-gating approach breaks the existing capture lifecycle in a way that requires broader architecture changes.

evidence: Task 1 local audit: normal capture depends on Screen Recording, while scroll capture additionally depends on Accessibility because rsnap forwards scroll into the target app and on Input Monitoring because rsnap installs a native CoreGraphics listen-event tap for global scroll-wheel input.
Task 2 outcome: apps/rsnap/src/permissions_macos.rs now preflights and requests Screen Recording, Accessibility, and Input Monitoring, and can open the corresponding macOS settings panes.

Task 2 outcome: apps/rsnap/src/app/capture.rs now blocks silent overlay startup when Screen Recording access is missing, opens Screen Recording settings when the one-shot prompt no longer appears, and defers scroll-capture-only permissions until the user explicitly enters scroll capture.

Task 2 outcome: apps/rsnap/src/settings_window/sections.rs and apps/rsnap/src/app/shell.rs now expose a persistent Permissions surface with one permission button per row plus tray/menubar recovery entrypoints.
Task 3 outcome: apps/rsnap/src/app.rs and apps/rsnap/src/app/runtime.rs now open the Settings window at startup when Screen Recording is still missing and refresh the Settings UI while it is visible.
Task 3 outcome: README.md and docs/spec/v0.md now describe the actual macOS permission contract instead of claiming Accessibility or Input Monitoring are never needed.
Task 4 verification: cargo make checks exited 0 in .workspaces/xy-167-permission-gate.
Task 4 verification: RSNAP_BUNDLE_OPEN_APP=0 scripts/bundle-macos.sh rebuilt target/release/bundle/osx/Rsnap.app in .workspaces/xy-167-permission-gate.
Task 4 verification: the current permission-gate lane also passes cargo check -p rsnap before the full repo-native gate.
